name: Kettlebell Press
description: The kettlebell press is a unilateral overhead pressing exercise performed from the kettlebell rack position, pressing the bell directly overhead to full arm lockout. The offset center of mass of the kettlebell compared to a dumbbell requires greater forearm and wrist stability to control the bell path. As a strict press with no leg drive, it isolates the deltoid, triceps, and upper trapezius, while the unilateral nature demands significant anti-lateral flexion core engagement throughout.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Kettlebell in the rack position on the right side — bell resting on the forearm, elbow close to the body, upper arm vertical.
execution.setup_instructions: Clean the kettlebell into the rack position to begin. Stand tall with the torso upright.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the racked position with the bell at shoulder height, elbow close to the torso.
Step 2: Press the kettlebell directly overhead by extending the elbow and driving the hand upward.
Step 3: Lock out the arm fully overhead — the bicep should be near the ear.
Step 4: Lower the bell under control back to the rack position.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press. Inhale on the return to rack.
common_mistakes: Side-bending away from the bell — maintain an upright torso
Not fully locking out the elbow at the top
Starting with the elbow flared out — it should be close to the body in the rack
safety_considerations: Shoulder impingement or instability should be assessed before heavy overhead pressing.
Ensure full lockout on each rep to protect the shoulder joint.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow lockout overhead. Full return to racked position.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3–8 reps per side. Controlled tempo — 2 seconds up, pause at top, 2 seconds down.
coaching_cues: Lock out — bicep near the ear
